title: 6. 12-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet Audit
book_title: Chapter 6: Twelve Years of Numbers — ROCE Decay, Working Capital & The Debt Reset

epigraph.quote: Profitability is an opinion until it clears the working-capital cycle and shows up on the balance sheet without a matching pile of debt.
epigraph.author: Balance Sheet Forensics

summary: Across twelve years (FY15–FY26), Cyient grew sales from ₹2,736 Cr to ₹7,268 Cr (and ₹8,086 Cr TTM), but 5-year sales growth slowed to 12.0% and ROCE compressed from 25% in FY15 and 22% in FY24 to 12.3% in FY26. Simultaneously, the Cash Conversion Cycle swung from negative (-337 days in FY16) to +119 days in FY26 due to DLM's 303-day inventory profile, and the September 2026 balance sheet recorded a 6.4x jump in borrowings to ₹2,759 Cr.

web_blocks.html: Cyient's twelve-year financial record (FY15 through FY26, plus TTM and September 2026) falls into two distinct regimes [1]. The business compounded steadily through FY24, hit a two-year plateau in FY25–FY26, and then reshaped its capital base in H1 FY27 [1].

web_blocks.caption: Cyient Consolidated Profit & Loss (FY15 – TTM Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sales expanded 2.66x from ₹2,736 Cr (FY15) to ₹7,268 Cr (FY26) and ₹8,086 Cr (TTM), but Net Profit in FY26 (₹463 Cr) and TTM (₹404 Cr) sits well below the FY24 peak of ₹703 Cr due to OPM compression and rising interest/tax.

web_blocks.caption: Cyient Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY15 – Sep 2026, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: The September 2026 column captures the structural break: Borrowings jumped from ₹431 Cr to ₹2,759 Cr, Fixed Assets nearly doubled from ₹3,084 Cr to ₹6,021 Cr (Kinetic + TAO Digital), and Equity+Reserves fell from ₹5,682 Cr to ₹5,098 Cr (₹720 Cr buyback).

web_blocks.caption: Cyient Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY15 – FY26, ₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cash conversion remains Cyient's strongest forensic anchor: CFO averaged ₹768 Cr/year across FY24–FY26, with FY26 CFO/EBITDA at 118% and Free Cash Flow at ₹693 Cr.

web_blocks.caption: Cyient Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY15 – FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: ROCE halved from 22% (FY24) to 12% (FY26) while Cash Conversion Cycle widened to 119–128 days as DLM inventory days climbed to 303.

web_blocks.caption: 12-Year Capital Efficiency & Leverage Trajectory (FY15 – Sep 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cyient's 12-year arc shows two clear regimes: a pre-FY24 asset-light services compounder (20–25% ROCE, negative CCC) and a post-FY24 manufacturing/M&A hybrid (12% ROCE, +119-day CCC, 0.54x D/E).

web_blocks.takeaway: Receivable discipline (66 debtor days) and operating cash flow (₹787 Cr) remain genuinely healthy, but return on capital (12.3% ROCE, 8.61% ROE) and true debt-like leverage (~₹3,686 Cr or 0.72x equity including TAO contingent earnouts) have deteriorated sharply.

web_blocks.html: Forensic Deep-Dive: Earnouts, M&A Friction & Deleveraging Math: Automated screens warn that Cyient "might be capitalizing interest cost" as Fixed Assets grow [1]. CWIP stayed small at ₹5 Cr in March 2026 and ₹12 Cr in September 2026 [1]. Yet footnotes expose two bigger overhangs. First, Other Liabilities jumped ₹1,590 Cr (+74%) in six months—from ₹2,137 Cr to ₹3,727 Cr [1][2]. That surge reflects ₹926.80 Cr of TAO Digital contingent earnouts on top of ₹1,229.50 Cr paid upfront [2]. Combined with ₹2,759 Cr of gross debt, total debt-like load hits ~₹3,686 Cr (~0.72x equity). Even reported gearing (0.54x) exceeds CRISIL's June 9, 2026 <0.50x medium-term cap [3]. Second, FY26 accounts absorbed ₹71.2 Cr of aborted-M&A fees and ₹27.8 Cr of goodwill impairment [4]. With ₹5,098 Cr equity and ₹6,021 Cr Fixed Assets/intangibles, Cyient needs ₹800–900 Cr in yearly FCF to pay dividends, settle earnouts, and cut debt without dilution [1].

web_blocks.title: Why Inventory Days Hit 303 While Debtor Days Stayed at 66
paragraphs: In a pure software or ER&D services company, Inventory Days are zero. Cyient's consolidated Inventory Days rose from 177 in FY24 to 303 in FY26 because Screener's ratio divides year-end DLM/manufacturing inventory by cost of materials consumed—and DLM has been stocking long-lead aerospace and defense components ahead of its 1.6x+ book-to-bill ramp.
Meanwhile, Debtor Days remained rock-steady at 66 days (versus 71 days in FY15 and 64 in FY24), confirming that Cyient is not inflating DET revenue via uncollected bills.

book_paragraphs: Now let us put twelve years of Cyient's financial statements side by side, because a single quarter never tells the whole truth. From March 2015 to March 2024, Cyient looked like a textbook mid-cap compounder: sales grew from ₹2,736 Cr to ₹7,147 Cr, net profit doubled from ₹351 Cr to ₹703 Cr, and Return on Capital Employed consistently stayed between 20% and 25% outside the COVID dip in FY20–FY21.

Over the last two years, however, that compounding engine stalled. Sales flattened at ₹7,360 Cr in FY25 and ₹7,268 Cr in FY26, while net profit fell by a third to ₹463 Cr—and ₹404 Cr on a trailing twelve-month basis—weighed down in FY26 not only by margin compression and the ₹42.3 Cr Labour Code charge, but also by ₹71.2 Cr of expenses on an aborted acquisition and ₹27.8 Cr of tooling goodwill impairment. As a result, Cyient's five-year sales growth stands at a modest 12.0%, its three-year ROE sits at 12.8% (and trailing ROE at just 8.61%), and its ROCE has dropped from 22% in FY24 to 12.3% today.

Look closely at the working capital ratios, because they explain a lot of that ROCE squeeze. In FY16, Cyient ran a negative Cash Conversion Cycle of minus 337 days. By FY26, the Cash Conversion Cycle had swung to plus 119 days, and Working Capital Days rose from 43 in FY24 to 68 in FY26. Why? Not because clients stopped paying—Debtor Days stayed remarkably disciplined at 66 days—but because Cyient DLM and Semiconductors carry physical inventory, pushing Inventory Days to 303 as DLM stocked aerospace components for its record order book.

Even so, Cyient's cash flow statement deserves respect. Through all the margin compression of FY25 and FY26, Cash from Operations held rock-steady at ₹790 Cr and ₹787 Cr respectively, converting 118% of FY26 EBITDA into operating cash flow and generating ₹693 Cr of Free Cash Flow. That cash discipline is the primary reason Cyient has been able to maintain a 42–56% dividend payout ratio for seven consecutive years.

Which brings us back to the September 2026 balance sheet—and a crucial footnote detail that headline debt ratios miss. Total Assets jumped from ₹8,250 Cr in March 2026 to ₹11,585 Cr in September 2026, driven by ₹2,937 Cr of new Fixed Assets and intangibles from Kinetic Technologies and TAO Digital. Reported gross borrowings surged from ₹431 Cr to ₹2,759 Cr (0.54x equity—already above the under-0.50x medium-term gearing benchmark in CRISIL's June 2026 rating rationale). Just as important, Other Liabilities jumped by ₹1,590 Cr to ₹3,727 Cr, reflecting ₹926.80 Cr of contingent earnout obligations for TAO Digital on top of the ₹1,229.50 Cr upfront payment. Combine gross borrowings with TAO's contingent earnouts and total debt-like obligations sit near ₹3,686 Cr (~0.72x equity).

Over the next eight quarters, Cyient's financial story boils down to simple deleveraging math: can its ₹700+ Cr annual free cash flow engine, reinforced by TAO Digital and Kinetic, fund both its dividend payout, its ₹926.80 Cr earnout obligations, and steady retirement of that ₹2,759 Cr debt pile so ROCE climbs back above 15%?

book_callouts.title: Clean Receivables vs. Leveraged Balance Sheet
book_callouts.text: The forensic audit gives you a split verdict: Cyient's revenue quality and cash collection are clean (66 debtor days, 118% CFO/EBITDA), so there is no sign of accounting fabrication. The risk is purely economic—lower returns on capital (12.3% ROCE) paired with a newly leveraged balance sheet (0.54x debt-to-equity).

book_subsections.title: What Must Go Right in FY27–FY28
paragraphs: For Cyient to earn its way back to compounder status, three metrics must improve together over the next four quarters: DET EBIT margin needs to hold above 14–15%, consolidated interest coverage must stay comfortable as full-year debt service hits the P&L, and gross borrowings need to trend down from ₹2,759 Cr.

If revenue growth from TAO Digital (~$80M run-rate) and Cyient Semiconductors (+240% YoY in Q2 FY27) translates into consolidated Free Cash Flow above ₹800–900 Cr, the leverage inflection will resolve cleanly. If margins slip back toward 12%, debt service and goodwill amortization will keep ROE trapped in single digits.
